u.n: Least-Privilege Validation — Interactive Logons to Database Tier from Workstations (PCI DSS Req 7.2.5, 8.2.1)
u.v: Surfaces database interactive logins from non-administrator workstations that may violate least privilege for personnel access to cardholder data stores.
u.t: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft SQL Server (2648) if audit ingested
u.d: `index=db` `mssql:audit` action="AUDIT SESSION" or `sourcetype="oracle:audit"`; `lookup pci_jump_hosts.csv` client IP
u.q:
index=db sourcetype="mssql:audit" earliest=-24h
| where match(action,"(?i)login|authentication")
| lookup pci_jump_hosts.csv ip AS client_ip OUTPUT is_jump
| where isnull(is_jump) OR is_jump="false"
| lookup pci_db_tier.csv server_name OUTPUT tier
| where tier="carddata_db"
| stats count by client_ip, server_name, database_principal_name
| sort - count
u.m: (1) Populate jump host egress IPs. (2) Exclude application service accounts via lookup. (3) Pair with bastion session logs for false positives. (4) Quarterly access review input.
u.z: Table (client_ip, principal), geomap, bar (count by server_name).
u.kfp: Administrative tasks, scheduled jobs or platform updates can match this pattern — correlate with change management, maintenance windows and user role before raising severity.
u.refs: [Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/742), [Splunk Add-on for Microsoft SQL Server](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/2648), [CIM: Authentication](https://docs.splunk.com/Documentation/CIM/latest/User/Authentication)
u.md:
Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft SQL Server (2648) if audit ingested.
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `index=db` `mssql:audit` action="AUDIT SESSION" or `sourcetype="oracle:audit"`; `lookup pci_jump_hosts.csv` client IP.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Populate jump host egress IPs. (2) Exclude application service accounts via lookup. (3) Pair with bastion session logs for false positives. (4) Quarterly access review input.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=db sourcetype="mssql:audit" earliest=-24h
| where match(action,"(?i)login|authentication")
| lookup pci_jump_hosts.csv ip AS client_ip OUTPUT is_jump
| where isnull(is_jump) OR is_jump="false"
| lookup pci_db_tier.csv server_name OUTPUT tier
| where tier="carddata_db"
| stats count by client_ip, server_name, database_principal_name
| sort - count
```

Understanding this SPL

u.n: Shared and Break-Glass Account Usage on Payment Infrastructure (PCI DSS Req 8.2.6, 8.6.1)
u.v: Tracks authentications to shared admin or break-glass accounts on in-scope systems so unique identification requirements are enforced except for documented emergency scenarios.
u.t: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742), Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (833)

 OR (index=linux sourcetype="linux:secure" earliest=-24h)

| lookup pci_shared_accounts.csv account AS acct OUTPUT shared_flag
| where shared_flag="true"
| lookup pci_in_scope_hosts.csv host OUTPUT in_scope
| where in_scope="true"
| stats values(src_ip) as src_ips, count by acct, host
| sort - count

u.n: Inactive Human Accounts Still Entitled to CDE Groups (PCI DSS Req 8.2.5, 8.2.6)

| where idle_days>90 AND NOT match(samAccountName,"(?i)^svc-")
| table samAccountName, idle_days, lastLogonTimestamp, department, manager
| sort - idle_days

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Build LDAP snapshot forwarder with `lastLogonTimestamp`. (2) Align 90-day threshold to corporate policy. (3) Auto-disable workflow in IAM integration. (4) Monthly PCI access review attachment.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=windows sourcetype="ad:user_snapshot" earliest=-2d
| lookup pci_cde_ad_groups.csv memberOf OUTPUT in_cde_group
| where in_cde_group="true"
| eval idle_days=round((now()-lastLogonTimestamp)/86400,1)
| where idle_days>90 AND NOT match(samAccountName,"(?i)^svc-")
| table samAccountName, idle_days, lastLogonTimestamp, department, manager
| sort - idle_days
```

| stats earliest(eval(if(src="app",_time,null()))) as t_app, earliest(eval(if(src="db",_time,null()))) as t_db by correlation_id

| where skew_sec>5 AND isnotnull(t_app) AND isnotnull(t_db)

| where p95_skew>5

| head 100

u.t: Splunk Enterprise / HEC
u.q:
index=privacy sourcetype="hipaa:breach_subject" earliest=-365d included_in_count="true"
| stats dc(subject_token) as affected by incident_id, state
| lookup state_media_threshold.csv state OUTPUT threshold
| eval media_needed=if(affected>=threshold,"Yes","No")
| where media_needed="Yes"

• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Palo Alto Networks Add-on for Splunk (Splunkbase 2757), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (Splunkbase 1621).
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `pan:traffic`, `pan:threat` or CIM Network_Traffic / Intrusion_Detection sources.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Fix timestamp parsing per TA — sample `last` field; (2) tune gap threshold per HA pair; (3) alert if firewall stops logging; (4) map to firewall inventory CM-8.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=net (sourcetype=pan:traffic OR sourcetype=pan:threat) earliest=-24h
| stats earliest(_time) as first, latest(_time) as last, count by host, sourcetype
| eval gap_minutes=round((now()-strptime(last,"%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %z"))/60,1)
| eval gap_minutes=if(isnull(gap_minutes), round((now()-last)/60,1), gap_minutes)
| where gap_minutes>30
```

Understanding this SPL

**Audit Generation Coverage for Critical Network Controls (AU-12)** — Verifies that boundary devices continue generating audit records for allow/deny decisions, evidencing AU-12 audit generation for network events.

Documented **Data sources**: `pan:traffic`, `pan:threat` or CIM Network_Traffic / Intrusion_Detection sources. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Palo Alto Networks Add-on for Splunk (Splunkbase 2757), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (Splunkbase 1621). The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: net; **sourcetype**: pan:traffic, pan:threat. Those sourcetypes align with what this use case lists under Data sources.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=net, sourcetype=pan:traffic, time bounds. Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by host, sourcetype** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions (useful for per-host, per-user, or per-entity comparisons for this use case).
• `eval` defines or adjusts **gap_minutes** — often to normalize units, derive a ratio, or prepare for thresholds.

u.n: Alternate Audit Capability During Control Outages (AU-15)
u.v: Detects when primary logging pipelines fail and compensating syslog or packet capture taps increase, evidencing AU-15 alternate audit capability activation.
u.t: Splunk Add-on for Stream (Splunkbase 1809), Splunk Connect for Syslog
u.q:
index=_internal OR index=net earliest=-24h
| eval channel=case(match(sourcetype,"stream"),"PCAP_TAP", match(sourcetype,"syslog"),"SYSLOG_ALT",1=1,"PRIMARY")
| bin _time span=15m
| stats sum(eval(if(channel="PRIMARY",1,0))) as primary_hits,
        sum(eval(if(channel!="PRIMARY",1,0))) as alt_hits by _time, host
| eval alt_ratio=round(alt_hits/(primary_hits+alt_hits+0.001),3)
| where alt_ratio>0.3
u.m: (1) Label alternate paths consistently; (2) tune ratio for your architecture; (3) require ticket linkage when alt_ratio spikes; (4) review monthly with contingency tests (CP-10).
u.z: Time chart (alt_ratio), Table (hosts), Single value (minutes in compensating mode)

u.n: IACS Incident Response Containment Interval (IEC 62443-2-1 / 4.3.4.5)
u.v: Quantifies detection-to-containment for OT cyber incidents and separates drills from production to evidence an exercised IR plan.

index=ot_incidents sourcetype="snow:incident" earliest=-180d
| where category="OT/Cyber" OR match(short_description,"(?i)ics|scada|plc")

u.n: Forced Remote Engineering Session Termination After Hours (IEC 62443-3-3 / SR 2.6)
u.v: Ensures vendor and internal remote sessions to OT are closed at shift end by correlating still-active tunnels with schedule.
u.t: Palo Alto (2757), CyberArk (4295)
u.q:
index=fw sourcetype="pan:traffic" earliest=-2d
| where app IN ("ssl","sslvpn","gp-gateway") AND dest_zone="OT-Jump"
| eval sess_key=concat(src,"-",dest_ip)
| stats min(_time) as start, max(_time) as end by sess_key, user
| eval span_h=(end-start)/3600
| eval ended_after_shift=if((strftime(end,"%H")>"22" OR strftime(end,"%H")<"05") AND span_h>4,1,0)
| where ended_after_shift=1
| table start, end, span_h, sess_key, user

u.n: Engineering Workstation Access Control — RDP Skips Jump Tier (IEC 62443-3-2 / Engineering workstation access control)
u.v: Alerts when RDP/WinRM sessions skip the jump tier and land directly on low-Purdue controllers or Windows I/O servers.
u.t: Windows + firewall
u.q:
(index=windows EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10 host="PLC-WIN-IO-*") OR (index=fw sourcetype="pan:traffic" app="rdp" dest_zone="OT-L1")
| eval session_key=coalesce(src_ip, src)
| lookup ot_jump_required.csv dest_ip OUTPUT jump_required
| where jump_required="true"
| stats count by user, dest_ip, host
| sort - count
u.m: (1) Disable RDP on controllers; (2) enforce PSM-only path; (3) GPO firewall; (4) weekly exception report.

Prerequisites

• Ensure the following data sources are available: `WinEventLog:Security` 4624 type=10; `pan:traffic` rdp.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Disable RDP on controllers; (2) enforce PSM-only path; (3) GPO firewall; (4) weekly exception report.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
(index=windows EventCode=4624 Logon_Type=10 host="PLC-WIN-IO-*") OR (index=fw sourcetype="pan:traffic" app="rdp" dest_zone="OT-L1")
| eval session_key=coalesce(src_ip, src)
| lookup ot_jump_required.csv dest_ip OUTPUT jump_required
| where jump_required="true"
| stats count by user, dest_ip, host
| sort - count
```

Understanding this SPL

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: windows, fw; **sourcetype**: pan:traffic; **host** filter: PLC-WIN-IO-*. That sourcetype matches what this use case lists under Data sources.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=windows, index=fw, sourcetype="pan:traffic". Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.

• Enriches events using `lookup` (lookup definition + optional OUTPUT fields).
• Filters the current rows with `where jump_required="true"` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.

• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Active Directory (3207), Splunk DB Connect (2686), Splunk Add-on for ServiceNow (1928), Splunk ITSI (1841), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621)..
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `WinEventLog:Security`, Active Directory replication/audit, `snow:*`, SAP/Oracle audit, `mssql:audit`, PAM, backup jobs.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Confirm field extractions and CIM tags for the sourcetypes in scope; (2) Load or maintain the referenced lookups/KVStore collections with owner attestation dates; (3) Schedule the search at an interval aligned to the control’s materiality; (4) Route positive findings to the compliance ticketing queue with required evidence fields; (5) Retain scheduled search exports per records management and legal hold procedures.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication by Authentication.dest | sort - count
```

Understanding this SPL

**User provisioning evidence tied to financial application accounts (SOX §404 / COSO)** — Supports SOX IT general and application controls evidence for "User provisioning evidence tied to financial application accounts" by correlating security, change, ERP, and ITSM telemetry with control ownership records, strengthening SOX §404 / COSO attestation.

Documented **Data sources**: `WinEventLog:Security`, Active Directory replication/audit, `snow:*`, SAP/Oracle audit, `mssql:audit`, PAM, backup jobs. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Active Directory (3207), Splunk DB Connect (2686), Splunk Add-on for ServiceNow (1928), Splunk ITSI (1841), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621). The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Uses `tstats` against accelerated summaries for data model `Authentication.Authentication` — enable acceleration for that model.
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.

Enable Data Model Acceleration (and metric indexes for `mstats`) for the models or datasets referenced above; otherwise `tstats`/`mstats` may return no results from summaries.


Step 3 — Validate
Confirm that events are present in the index and that the search returns expected results. Compare with known good/bad scenarios if applicable. Verify field extractions and index permissions.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Time chart, Table, Single value, Bar chart

Prerequisites

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Confirm field extractions and CIM tags for the sourcetypes in scope; (2) Load or maintain the referenced lookups/KVStore collections with owner attestation dates; (3) Schedule the search at an interval aligned to the control’s materiality; (4) Route positive findings to the compliance ticketing queue with required evidence fields; (5) Retain scheduled search exports per records management and legal hold procedures.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication by Authentication.action, Authentication.user, Authentication.src | sort - count
```

Understanding this SPL

**Subledger-to-general-ledger reconciliation variance monitoring (SOX reconciliation)** — Supports SOX IT general and application controls evidence for "Subledger-to-general-ledger reconciliation variance monitoring" by correlating security, change, ERP, and ITSM telemetry with control ownership records, strengthening SOX reconciliation attestation.

The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Uses `tstats` against accelerated summaries for data model `Authentication.Authentication` — enable acceleration for that model.
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.

Enable Data Model Acceleration (and metric indexes for `mstats`) for the models or datasets referenced above; otherwise `tstats`/`mstats` may return no results from summaries.

Confirm that events are present in the index and that the search returns expected results. Compare with known good/bad scenarios if applicable. Verify field extractions and index permissions.

Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk OT Security Add-on (5151), Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk Add-on for Palo Alto Networks (2757), Splunk Industrial Asset Intelligence, Splunk Add-on for CyberArk (4295), Splunk Edge Hub, Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621)..
• Ensure the following data sources are available: `pan:traffic`, SCADA/HMI audit, PAM, `nozomi:alert`, NetFlow, ITSM, passive OT asset discovery.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Confirm field extractions and CIM tags for the sourcetypes in scope; (2) Load or maintain the referenced lookups/KVStore collections with owner attestation dates; (3) Schedule the search at an interval aligned to the control’s materiality; (4) Route positive findings to the compliance ticketing queue with required evidence fields; (5) Retain scheduled search exports per records management and legal hold procedures.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
| tstats summariesonly=t avg(All_Traffic.bytes_in) as agg_value from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic by All_Traffic.action, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port span=1mon | sort - agg_value
```

Understanding this SPL

**Monthly OT security posture score trend by site (TSA monitoring)** — Supports pipeline cybersecurity program oversight under TSA Pipeline Security Directive by correlating operational telemetry with governance records for "Monthly OT security posture score trend by site".

The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Uses `tstats` against accelerated summaries for data model `Network_Traffic.All_Traffic` — enable acceleration for that model.
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.

Enable Data Model Acceleration (and metric indexes for `mstats`) for the models or datasets referenced above; otherwise `tstats`/`mstats` may return no results from summaries.


Step 3 — Validate
Confirm that events are present in the index and that the search returns expected results. Compare with known good/bad scenarios if applicable. Verify field extractions and index permissions.

Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Time chart, Choropleth or site bar, Table, Single value

• Ensure the following data sources are available: RTU/PLC, DNP3, Modbus OPC-UA, Wonderware/Ignition, historian, OT firewall, wireless sensor feeds.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Confirm field extractions and CIM tags for the sourcetypes in scope; (2) Load or maintain the referenced lookups/KVStore collections with owner attestation dates; (3) Schedule the search at an interval aligned to the control’s materiality; (4) Route positive findings to the compliance ticketing queue with required evidence fields; (5) Retain scheduled search exports per records management and legal hold procedures.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic by All_Traffic.action, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port | sort - count
```

Understanding this SPL

**OPC-UA Write method without named approver (API RP 1164)** — Evidences API RP 1164 cybersecurity practices for pipeline SCADA using OT and engineering audit sources.

The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Uses `tstats` against accelerated summaries for data model `Network_Traffic.All_Traffic` — enable acceleration for that model.
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.

Enable Data Model Acceleration (and metric indexes for `mstats`) for the models or datasets referenced above; otherwise `tstats`/`mstats` may return no results from summaries.

Confirm that events are present in the index and that the search returns expected results. Compare with known good/bad scenarios if applicable. Verify field extractions and index permissions.

• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk OT Security Add-on (5151), Splunk Industrial Asset Intelligence, Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk Edge Hub, Nozomi Networks TA for Splunk (6905), Splunk Add-on for CyberArk (4295), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621)..
• Ensure the following data sources are available: RTU/PLC, DNP3, Modbus OPC-UA, Wonderware/Ignition, historian, OT firewall, wireless sensor feeds.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Confirm field extractions and CIM tags for the sourcetypes in scope; (2) Load or maintain the referenced lookups/KVStore collections with owner attestation dates; (3) Schedule the search at an interval aligned to the control’s materiality; (4) Route positive findings to the compliance ticketing queue with required evidence fields; (5) Retain scheduled search exports per records management and legal hold procedures.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic by All_Traffic.action, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest, All_Traffic.dest_port | sort - count
```

Understanding this SPL

**OPC-UA unsigned program downloads (API RP 1164)** — Evidences API RP 1164 cybersecurity practices for pipeline SCADA using OT and engineering audit sources.

Documented **Data sources**: RTU/PLC, DNP3, Modbus OPC-UA, Wonderware/Ignition, historian, OT firewall, wireless sensor feeds. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Splunk OT Security Add-on (5151), Splunk Industrial Asset Intelligence, Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk Edge Hub, Nozomi Networks TA for Splunk (6905), Splunk Add-on for CyberArk (4295), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621). The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Uses `tstats` against accelerated summaries for data model `Network_Traffic.All_Traffic` — enable acceleration for that model.
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.

Enable Data Model Acceleration (and metric indexes for `mstats`) for the models or datasets referenced above; otherwise `tstats`/`mstats` may return no results from summaries.


Step 3 — Validate
Confirm that events are present in the index and that the search returns expected results. Compare with known good/bad scenarios if applicable. Verify field extractions and index permissions.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Time chart, Table, Single value, Node-link or sankey (optional)

Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk DB Connect (2686), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742), Splunk ITSI (1841), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621)..
• Ensure the following data sources are available: LIMS, MES, ELN, CDS, QMS/ERP validation logs, Windows security for GxP workstations.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Confirm field extractions and CIM tags for the sourcetypes in scope; (2) Load or maintain the referenced lookups/KVStore collections with owner attestation dates; (3) Schedule the search at an interval aligned to the control’s materiality; (4) Route positive findings to the compliance ticketing queue with required evidence fields; (5) Retain scheduled search exports per records management and legal hold procedures.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Change.All_Changes by All_Changes.user | sort - count
```

Understanding this SPL

**ELN logins without FIDO2 or X.509 credential (21 CFR Part 11)** — Supports Part 11 technical controls evidence by correlating validated system audit trails with identity and change records.

Documented **Data sources**: LIMS, MES, ELN, CDS, QMS/ERP validation logs, Windows security for GxP workstations. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk DB Connect (2686), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742), Splunk ITSI (1841), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621). The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Uses `tstats` against accelerated summaries for data model `Change.All_Changes` — enable acceleration for that model.
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.

Enable Data Model Acceleration (and metric indexes for `mstats`) for the models or datasets referenced above; otherwise `tstats`/`mstats` may return no results from summaries.


Step 3 — Validate
Confirm that events are present in the index and that the search returns expected results. Compare with known good/bad scenarios if applicable. Verify field extractions and index permissions.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Time chart, Table, Single value

Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk Add-on for AWS (1876), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services (3110), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742), Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (833), Splunk Add-on for Tenable (4060), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621)..
• Ensure the following data sources are available: CloudTrail, Azure Monitor, Tenable/STIG scans, POA&M exports, AAD/O365 sign-in, inventory.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Confirm field extractions and CIM tags for the sourcetypes in scope; (2) Load or maintain the referenced lookups/KVStore collections with owner attestation dates; (3) Schedule the search at an interval aligned to the control’s materiality; (4) Route positive findings to the compliance ticketing queue with required evidence fields; (5) Retain scheduled search exports per records management and legal hold procedures.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
| tstats summariesonly=t dc(Authentication.dest) as agg_value from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication by Authentication.action, Authentication.user, Authentication.src | sort - agg_value
```

Understanding this SPL

**Tenable FedRAMP compliance failures (FISMA / FedRAMP)** — Strengthens agency or cloud service continuous authorization evidence under FISMA / FedRAMP across cloud, endpoint, and GRC feeds.

Documented **Data sources**: CloudTrail, Azure Monitor, Tenable/STIG scans, POA&M exports, AAD/O365 sign-in, inventory. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk Add-on for AWS (1876), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services (3110), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742), Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (833), Splunk Add-on for Tenable (4060), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621). The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Uses `tstats` against accelerated summaries for data model `Authentication.Authentication` — enable acceleration for that model.
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.

Enable Data Model Acceleration (and metric indexes for `mstats`) for the models or datasets referenced above; otherwise `tstats`/`mstats` may return no results from summaries.


Step 3 — Validate
Confirm that events are present in the index and that the search returns expected results. Compare with known good/bad scenarios if applicable. Verify field extractions and index permissions.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Time chart, Table, Single value, Heat map

• Ensure the following data sources are available: CloudTrail, Azure Monitor, Tenable/STIG scans, POA&M exports, AAD/O365 sign-in, inventory.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Confirm field extractions and CIM tags for the sourcetypes in scope; (2) Load or maintain the referenced lookups/KVStore collections with owner attestation dates; (3) Schedule the search at an interval aligned to the control’s materiality; (4) Route positive findings to the compliance ticketing queue with required evidence fields; (5) Retain scheduled search exports per records management and legal hold procedures.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication by Authentication.action, Authentication.user, Authentication.src | sort - count
```

Understanding this SPL

**FedRAMP POA&M items past planned finish (FISMA / FedRAMP)** — Strengthens agency or cloud service continuous authorization evidence under FISMA / FedRAMP across cloud, endpoint, and GRC feeds.

Documented **Data sources**: CloudTrail, Azure Monitor, Tenable/STIG scans, POA&M exports, AAD/O365 sign-in, inventory. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk Add-on for AWS (1876), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services (3110), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742), Splunk Add-on for Unix and Linux (833), Splunk Add-on for Tenable (4060), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621). The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Uses `tstats` against accelerated summaries for data model `Authentication.Authentication` — enable acceleration for that model.
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.

Enable Data Model Acceleration (and metric indexes for `mstats`) for the models or datasets referenced above; otherwise `tstats`/`mstats` may return no results from summaries.


Step 3 — Validate
Confirm that events are present in the index and that the search returns expected results. Compare with known good/bad scenarios if applicable. Verify field extractions and index permissions.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Time chart, Table, Single value, Heat map

Step 1 — Configure data collection

```spl
| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Authentication.Authentication by Authentication.dest | sort - count
```

• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.

Confirm that events are present in the index and that the search returns expected results. Compare with known good/bad scenarios if applicable. Verify field extractions and index permissions.

index=aml sourcetype="aml:sar:event" earliest=-7d
| eval aml_tag="sar_time"

| bin _time span=1h

| eventstats perc95(amount_eur) as p95_amt by aml_tag

| head 300

• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742), Splunk ITSI (1841), Splunk Add-on for AWS (1876), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services (3110), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621).
• Ensure the following data sources are available: Windows Security Event Logs, cloud audit trails (AWS, Azure), network infrastructure logs, financial application logs, identity management systems, vulnerability scan outputs, incident response logs, operational resilience evidence.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Maintain `uk_oes_inventory.csv` with OES identifiers, essential services, and CAF mappings. (2) Tag correlation searches with `nis_relevant` or `fca_relevant` for workflow routing. (3) Integrate IR ticketing milestones for competent authority and FCA clocks. (4) Monthly review with compliance, technology risk, and resilience forums.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" earliest=-34h EventCode IN (4624,4625,4648)
| lookup uk_oes_assets.csv host OUTPUT oes_tier
| where isnotnull(oes_tier)
| stats dc(IpAddress) as src_ips, count by user, host, oes_tier
| where count>100
| sort - count
```

Understanding this SPL

index=itsi_summary service_title="*Payments*" earliest=-7d

| where hs<85

Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk ITSI (1841), Splunk Add-on for AWS (1876), Splunk DB Connect (2686), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621).
• Ensure the following data sources are available: Banking system audit trails, cloud infrastructure logs, vulnerability scan outputs, privileged access management logs, change management records, business continuity evidence, incident response logs, outsourcing management records.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Maintain `apac_material_services.csv` for important business services and regulator tags. (2) Send weekly digests to CRO and technology risk committees. (3) Validate DB Connect concurrency for audit peak windows. (4) Archive results to a restricted summary index for retention governance.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=vendor sourcetype="mas:outsourcing" earliest=-180d
| stats latest(risk_rating) as rr by vendor_name
| where rr IN ("High","Severe")
```

Understanding this SPL

**Outsourcing arrangements risk monitoring (MAS TRM)** — Supports MAS TRM supervisory examination readiness for outsourcing arrangements risk monitoring.

Documented **Data sources**: Banking system audit trails, cloud infrastructure logs, vulnerability scan outputs, privileged access management logs, change management records, business continuity evidence, incident response logs, outsourcing management records. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk ITSI (1841), Splunk Add-on for AWS (1876), Splunk DB Connect (2686), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621). The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: vendor; **sourcetype**: mas:outsourcing. If that sourcetype is not mentioned in Data sources, double-check parsing or update the documentation to match the feed you actually ingest.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=vendor, sourcetype="mas:outsourcing", time bounds. Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by vendor_name** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions (useful for per-host, per-user, or per-entity comparisons for this use case).
• Filters the current rows with `where rr IN ("High","Severe")` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

index=vendor sourcetype="rbi:vendor_risk" earliest=-90d

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Maintain `apac_material_services.csv` for important business services and regulator tags. (2) Send weekly digests to CRO and technology risk committees. (3) Validate DB Connect concurrency for audit peak windows. (4) Archive results to a restricted summary index for retention governance.

Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=board sourcetype="cps234:board_report" earliest=-400d
| stats latest(submitted) as s by quarter
| where s!="true"
```

• Scopes the data: index=board, sourcetype="cps234:board_report", time bounds. Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.

• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742), Splunk Add-on for CrowdStrike FDR (5082), Splunk ITSI (1841), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621).
• Ensure the following data sources are available: Windows Security Event Logs, endpoint protection logs, cloud audit trails, vulnerability scan outputs, email security logs, network infrastructure logs, identity management systems, incident response records.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Ingest CrowdStrike policy posture via TA 5082 and map hosts to NDB and NZISM tiers. (2) Tune alerts with ACSD Essential Eight and APRA-aligned severities. (3) Coordinate privacy and security ownership for dual-reporting workflows. (4) Monthly export for privacy officer and prudential working groups.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=privacy sourcetype="pia:app" earliest=-730d
| stats latest(status) as st by app_id
| where st!="Complete" AND data_categories="health"
```

Understanding this SPL

**Privacy impact assessment register tracking (Privacy Act 1988 (Cth); NDB)** — Evidences Privacy Act 1988 (Cth); NDB obligations for privacy impact assessment register tracking using endpoint, identity, and cloud telemetry.

Documented **Data sources**: Windows Security Event Logs, endpoint protection logs, cloud audit trails, vulnerability scan outputs, email security logs, network infrastructure logs, identity management systems, incident response records. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742), Splunk Add-on for CrowdStrike FDR (5082), Splunk ITSI (1841), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621). The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: privacy; **sourcetype**: pia:app. If that sourcetype is not mentioned in Data sources, double-check parsing or update the documentation to match the feed you actually ingest.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=privacy, sourcetype="pia:app", time bounds. Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by app_id** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions (useful for per-host, per-user, or per-entity comparisons for this use case).
• Filters the current rows with `where st!="Complete" AND data_categories="health"` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.

Optional CIM / accelerated variant (same use case, normalized fields via Common Information Model):

```spl
| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes by Processes.process_name, Processes.user, Processes.dest | sort - count
```

Understanding this CIM / accelerated SPL

**Privacy impact assessment register tracking (Privacy Act 1988 (Cth); NDB)** — Evidences Privacy Act 1988 (Cth); NDB obligations for privacy impact assessment register tracking using endpoint, identity, and cloud telemetry.

Documented **Data sources**: Windows Security Event Logs, endpoint protection logs, cloud audit trails, vulnerability scan outputs, email security logs, network infrastructure logs, identity management systems, incident response records. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742), Splunk Add-on for CrowdStrike FDR (5082), Splunk ITSI (1841), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621). The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

This **CIM or accelerated** block uses normalized field names and/or `tstats` over data models. Enable **acceleration** on the referenced models (and correct CIM knowledge objects) or the search may return nothing.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Uses `tstats` against accelerated summaries for data model `Endpoint.Processes` — enable acceleration for that model.
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.

Enable Data Model Acceleration (and metric indexes for `mstats`) for the models or datasets referenced above; otherwise `tstats`/`mstats` may return no results from summaries.


Step 3 — Validate
Confirm that events are present in the index and that the search returns expected results. Compare with known good/bad scenarios if applicable. Verify field extractions and index permissions.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Single value (% compliant hosts), Bar chart (fails by control), Table (worst hosts).

• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742), Splunk Add-on for CrowdStrike FDR (5082), Splunk ITSI (1841), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621).
• Ensure the following data sources are available: Windows Security Event Logs, endpoint protection logs, cloud audit trails, vulnerability scan outputs, email security logs, network infrastructure logs, identity management systems, incident response records.
• For app installation, inputs.conf, and Splunk directory layout, see the Implementation guide: docs/implementation-guide.md

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Ingest CrowdStrike policy posture via TA 5082 and map hosts to NDB and NZISM tiers. (2) Tune alerts with ACSD Essential Eight and APRA-aligned severities. (3) Coordinate privacy and security ownership for dual-reporting workflows. (4) Monthly export for privacy officer and prudential working groups.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=wineventlog sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security" EventCode=4673 earliest=-24h
| stats count by ProcessName, ServiceName
| lookup asd_e8_scope.csv host OUTPUT in_scope
| where in_scope="true"
```

Understanding this SPL

**User application hardening compliance (ASD Essential Eight)** — Evidences ASD Essential Eight obligations for user application hardening compliance using endpoint, identity, and cloud telemetry.

Documented **Data sources**: Windows Security Event Logs, endpoint protection logs, cloud audit trails, vulnerability scan outputs, email security logs, network infrastructure logs, identity management systems, incident response records. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742), Splunk Add-on for CrowdStrike FDR (5082), Splunk ITSI (1841), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621). The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

The first pipeline stage scopes events using **index**: wineventlog; **sourcetype**: WinEventLog:Security. If that sourcetype is not mentioned in Data sources, double-check parsing or update the documentation to match the feed you actually ingest.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=wineventlog, sourcetype="WinEventLog:Security", time bounds. Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.
• `stats` rolls up events into metrics; results are split **by ProcessName, ServiceName** so each row reflects one combination of those dimensions (useful for per-host, per-user, or per-entity comparisons for this use case).
• Enriches events using `lookup` (lookup definition + optional OUTPUT fields).
• Filters the current rows with `where in_scope="true"` — typically the threshold or rule expression for this monitoring goal.

Optional CIM / accelerated variant (same use case, normalized fields via Common Information Model):

```spl
| tstats summariesonly=t count from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes by Processes.process_name, Processes.user, Processes.dest | sort - count
```

Understanding this CIM / accelerated SPL

**User application hardening compliance (ASD Essential Eight)** — Evidences ASD Essential Eight obligations for user application hardening compliance using endpoint, identity, and cloud telemetry.

Documented **Data sources**: Windows Security Event Logs, endpoint protection logs, cloud audit trails, vulnerability scan outputs, email security logs, network infrastructure logs, identity management systems, incident response records. **App/TA** (typical add-on context): Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742), Splunk Add-on for CrowdStrike FDR (5082), Splunk ITSI (1841), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621). The SPL below should target the same indexes and sourcetypes you configured for that feed—rename `index=` / `sourcetype=` if your deployment differs.

This **CIM or accelerated** block uses normalized field names and/or `tstats` over data models. Enable **acceleration** on the referenced models (and correct CIM knowledge objects) or the search may return nothing.

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Uses `tstats` against accelerated summaries for data model `Endpoint.Processes` — enable acceleration for that model.
• Orders rows with `sort` — combine with `head`/`tail` for top-N patterns.

Enable Data Model Acceleration (and metric indexes for `mstats`) for the models or datasets referenced above; otherwise `tstats`/`mstats` may return no results from summaries.


Step 3 — Validate
Confirm that events are present in the index and that the search returns expected results. Compare with known good/bad scenarios if applicable. Verify field extractions and index permissions.

Step 4 — Operationalize
Add the search to a dashboard or set up alert actions (email, webhook, PagerDuty, etc.) as required. Document the use case in your runbook and assign an owner. Consider visualizations: Single value (% compliant hosts), Bar chart (fails by control), Table (worst hosts).

Prerequisites
• Install and configure the required add-on or app: Splunk Enterprise Security (263), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742), Splunk Add-on for AWS (1876), Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Cloud Services (3110), Splunk Common Information Model Add-on (1621).
• Ensure the following data sources are available: Cloud audit trails, Windows Security Event Logs, vulnerability scan outputs, access control logs, encryption status reports, continuous monitoring feeds, incident response logs, privacy management platforms, law enforcement system logs.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Maintain `amer_authorization_boundary.csv` with ATO, CUI, and CJIS scope flags. (2) Integrate POA&M exports via scheduled output and lookup refresh for ISSM workflows. (3) Separate LGPD and federal datasets with index- and role-level controls. (4) Quarterly control mapping workshop with ISSM, ISO, and privacy counsel.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=cmp sourcetype="lgpd:consent" earliest=-90d
| stats latest(consent_status) as cs by data_subject_id, purpose_id
| where cs!="recorded"
```

Understanding this SPL

**Pipeline walkthrough**

• Scopes the data: index=cmp, sourcetype="lgpd:consent", time bounds. Cross-check against **Data sources** above so indexes and sourcetypes match your ingestion.

| eval missing=mvfilter(NOT match(acked_systems, system))
| where mvcount(missing)>0
| table ticket_id subject_token systems_in_scope acked_systems missing

u.n: Multi-regulator breach-notification SLA tracker (24h NIS2 / 72h GDPR / 72h HIPAA)
u.v: Most enforcement actions against supervisory breaches (ICO, DPC, BaFin) focus on notification timeliness. This UC turns the obligation into a visible KPI instead of a post-facto audit finding.
u.t: Splunk Enterprise / Splunk Cloud Platform
u.q:
| inputlookup incident_register.csv
| where classification="breach"
| eval applicable_regs=split(applicable_regs,",")
| mvexpand applicable_regs
| lookup sla_catalog.csv regulator as applicable_regs OUTPUT sla_hours
| eval deadline=strptime(classified_at,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ")+sla_hours*3600
| join incident_id applicable_regs [search index=notifications sourcetype=regulator:submission | fields incident_id applicable_regs tracking_id submitted_at]
| eval status=case(isnull(tracking_id) AND now()>deadline, "breach", isnull(tracking_id) AND (deadline-now())<5400, "imminent", isnotnull(tracking_id), "submitted")
| table incident_id applicable_regs deadline submitted_at status

index=_audit action=search info=completed earliest=-24h
| stats values(artifact_id) as artifact_ids earliest(_time) as first_seen latest(_time) as last_seen by search_id user
| mvexpand artifact_ids
| join type=outer artifact_ids [| rest /services/search/jobs splunk_server=* | fields sid dispatchState | rename sid as artifact_ids]

u.n: DORA Art.17 — ICT incident classification timeliness: major-incident clock evidence
u.v: Supervisors under DORA request the per-incident clock evidence. This UC produces it automatically, so the entity can prove the notification workflow was operated within the required windows or identify the exact root cause of a miss.
u.t: Splunk SOAR, Splunk Add-on for ServiceNow
u.d: `index=soar` sourcetype=servicenow:sir_incident OR sourcetype=phantom:incident; `index=ticketing` sourcetype=jira:issue (IR project); regulator notification log `index=compliance` sourcetype=dora:notification.
u.q:
index=soar sourcetype IN (servicenow:sir_incident,phantom:incident) tag::major_incident=true earliest=-1d
| stats min(detected_at) AS detected_at min(classified_at) AS classified_at min(notified_at) AS notified_at min(intermediate_at) AS intermediate_at min(final_at) AS final_at BY incident_id
| eval detect_to_classify_h=round((classified_at-detected_at)/3600,2)
| eval classify_to_initial_h=round((notified_at-classified_at)/3600,2)
| eval initial_to_inter_h=round((intermediate_at-notified_at)/3600,2)
| eval inter_to_final_h=round((final_at-intermediate_at)/3600,2)
| eval SLA_breached=if(detect_to_classify_h>24 OR classify_to_initial_h>24 OR initial_to_inter_h>72 OR inter_to_final_h>720,1,0)
| table incident_id detected_at classified_at notified_at intermediate_at final_at detect_to_classify_h classify_to_initial_h initial_to_inter_h inter_to_final_h SLA_breached
u.m: (1) Normalise detected_at/classified_at/notified_at/intermediate_at/final_at in the IR tool; (2) tag major incidents at classification; (3) schedule UC every 5m; (4) SLA_breached=1 escalates to CISO + Head of IR; (5) monthly roll-up to Board; (6) annual tabletop exercise validates clock fidelity.
u.z: Per-incident Gantt of phase durations, timechart of breaches per quarter, single value 'open incidents at risk of SLA breach in next 4h'.
u.kfp: Incidents re-classified as non-major after initial raise can show a misleading 'breach' until tag::major_incident is cleared — dedup on latest tag state before computing SLAs.

u.v: Gives the CISO and the ICT risk committee a single-query attestation that the operational-resilience testing programme executed as planned, replacing an email-based reconciliation that typically slips by weeks.

| eval on_time=if(actual_run_time<=planned_date_et+86400*14,1,0)
| table test_id test_type scope_service planned_date actual_run_time pass_fail finding_count evidence_complete on_time

u.n: ISO/IEC 27001:2022 Clause 7.2 — Competence evidence: role-based training completion
u.v: Replaces the annual LMS export with a daily compliance signal. HR can notify managers proactively rather than after the audit finding.
u.t: Splunk Add-on for Microsoft Windows (742)
u.q:
index=hr sourcetype=hr:role_assignment earliest=-30d
| stats latest(role) AS role BY user
| lookup iso_27001_training_matrix.csv role OUTPUT required_modules
| eval required_modules=split(required_modules,",")
| join user
  [search index=hr sourcetype=lms:completion status=completed earliest=-365d
   | stats values(module) AS completed_modules BY user]
| eval covered=mvmap(required_modules, if(isnotnull(mvfind(completed_modules,x)),1,0))
| eval compliance_pct=round(100*sum(covered)/mvcount(required_modules),0)
| where compliance_pct<100
| table user role required_modules completed_modules compliance_pct

u.kfp: New hires in their grace window (30d) appear as non-compliant — exclude by hire_date.

| where pan_match=1 OR cvv_match=1

u.n: PCI-DSS 10.7 — Log retention: CDE data-source retention + immutability attestation
u.v: Prevents the audit-killing discovery that retention was silently reduced during an index rebuild. Daily attestation beats the quarterly spot-check.
u.t: Splunk Enterprise / Splunk Cloud Platform
u.q:
| rest /services/data/indexes
| where match(title,"^(cde|pci)_")
| eval configured_days=round(frozenTimePeriodInSecs/86400,0)
| table title configured_days minTime maxTime
| rename title AS index
| eval oldest_event_age_d=round((now()-strptime(minTime,"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z"))/86400,0)
| join type=outer index
  [search index=compliance sourcetype=worm:signer earliest=-7d
   | stats latest(_time) AS worm_last_write BY index]
| where configured_days<365 OR oldest_event_age_d<365 OR worm_last_write<now()-86400
| table index configured_days oldest_event_age_d worm_last_write

u.z: Bar of retention days by index, table of gaps, single value 'indexes below 365d'.

u.n: NERC CIP-008-6 R1 incident response plan — evidence of activation and review
u.v: CIP-008-6 R1 requires an IR plan and evidence of activation / annual review. Automated tracking catches drift before a CIP enforcement action.

u.d: SOC ticketing, CIP incident reports, annual plan-review logs.
u.q:
index=soc_tickets sourcetype=cip:incident earliest=-365d
| eval plan_version=coalesce(plan_version,"unknown")

| eval days_since_review=round((now()-last_review)/86400,0)
| table bes_function, plan_version, incidents, first_activation, last_activation, days_since_review
| where days_since_review > 365 OR isnull(last_review)

Step 1 — Configure data collection
(1) Identify the SWIFT secure zone with a 'zone=swift' asset field; (2) route EDR logs through a dedicated source; (3) schedule daily.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
Run the following SPL in Search (then save as report or alert; adjust time range and threshold as needed):

```spl
index=swift_zone earliest=-24h
| search (sourcetype="av" OR sourcetype="edr")
| stats count AS events count(eval(signature_coverage_hours <= 24)) AS current_coverage count(eval(action="block")) AS blocks BY host, edr_vendor
| eval up_to_date=if(current_coverage=events, "yes", "no")
| where up_to_date="no" OR blocks > 0
```
